findings.title: Re-running an earlier stage's done is no longer treated as passed when history lags the files
quotes: if at(stage) < at(here["stage"]) and (rec is None or at(stage) < at(rec) and at(rec) >= at(here["stage"])):
A stage before both is already passed (FR-17).
findings.fix: revert the extra `and at(rec) >= at(here["stage"])` condition, or state why it is needed and add a test for it.

sources.situation: history's last `to` (rec) is behind the files' stage (FR-47 lag), and the caller runs `nio flow done` for a stage earlier than rec. The comment says it is before both and should print "is past ... nothing to do". The added `at(rec) >= at(here["stage"])` makes it fall through to the guard, so it can record a second pass line for an old stage. The lite path does not need this change, because after the grilling pass rec equals the stage where the effort stands.

findings.reason: src/nio/flow.py:974 now reads `at(stage) < at(here["stage"]) and (rec is None or at(stage) < at(rec) and at(rec) >= at(here["stage"]))`. When history lags the files (rec < here) and stage < rec, the old test returned "is past ... nothing to do", but the new one falls through to `guard` and a possible second pass line, against the comment "A stage before both is already passed (FR-17)". No test in tests/ asserts "is past", and nothing in the spec (FR-2, FR-15) or the T-1 commit message justifies the extra condition.

findings.title: The grill sends the human to a spec-skill section that does not exist
quotes: offers the full flow (@nio:spec, "Escalating a bug fix")

sources.situation: the escalation stop in step 4 tells the agent to offer the full flow by pointing to @nio:spec "Escalating a bug fix". grep finds no such section in skills/spec, so the agent has nothing to follow when an FR-8 trigger hits.

findings.fix: rename the test to match the epic case, e.g. `test_ac53_epic_unsupported`, and keep the TC-53 docstring.

sources.situation: the test name says a lite spec is unsupported, but after this diff lite is driven by the flow (CT-2) and the body asserts `unsupported: epic`. A reader searching for lite-unsupported behaviour finds a test that now checks the opposite.
